name: Duwai
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Schuh, Russell G. 1977 Bade/Ngizim determiner system + Schuh's Yobe Languages Research Project Duwai materials (aflang.linguistics.ucla.edu unreachable)

sources.citation: Daskum, Alhaji Abba (comp.). 2009. Terzena de Rawa Kunuk Tave Duwai [Duwai verbal arts with English translation]. Potiskum: Yobe Languages Research Project, 31 pp; and Kacalla, Buba (comp.). 2007. Duwai proverbs, 1 p.
sources.note: Text collections in practical orthography (no tone or length marking); no phonological notes.

sources.citation: Daskum, Alhaji Abba, with Buba Kachallah; Russell G. Schuh (ed.). 2009. Duwai-English-Hausa Dictionary (1st edition). Potiskum: Yobe Languages Research Project / Ajami Press. 58 pp.
sources.note: Introduction 'Duwai spelling' (pp. iii-vii) treats segments, contrastive vowel length and tone (H, L, downstepped H, falling, rising) as the features needed for correct pronunciation and meaning; word stress/accent is never mentioned.

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 2005. Yobe State, Nigeria as a linguistic area. BLS 31 (full ms. version); and Schuh 2005, The totality extension and focus in West Chadic (Berlin ms.).
sources.note: Duwai cited comparatively (lexicon, tone of numerals, second subjunctive); zero hits for stress/accent.

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 2002. Handout 02: Phonological overview (Bade/Ngizim/Duwai). Linguistics 252, UCLA, Winter 2002, 10 pp.
sources.note: Segmental inventories and sound correspondences including Duwai (laryngeals, liquids, palatalization, diphthong monophthongization); no stress or accent.

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. n.d. Western Bade phonology. Ms., UCLA, 28 pp.
sources.note: Western Bade only (sister language); zero hits for stress/accent.

sources.citation: UCLA African Languages / Yobe Languages Research Project, 'Duwai' page (aflang.humanities.ucla.edu) and archived.
sources.note: States: 'The only published work on Duwai is a wordlist in Sigismund Koelle, Polyglotta Africana (1854) and.. Schuh, Bade/Ngizim determiner system (1977)'; lists the 2008 verbal-system ms. as the only paper on Duwai and points to the 2009 dictionary. (Page.)

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 2008. The Duwai verbal system. Ms., UCLA, 8 pp. (drafted 1974 in Gashua, typed 2007, revised after 2007 fieldwork).
sources.note: SS1.2 'Verbal tone' and SS1.3 'Tone rules' (p. 2): verb tone entirely determined by TAM; H SPREADING and L SPREADING rules. No mention of stress or accent anywhere (the only 'accent' is 'circumflex accent indicating falling tone', p. 5).

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 2002. Bade and Ngizim phonology and morphology: References (Linguistics 252 bibliography), 2 pp; and archived course page.
sources.note: Bibliographic: lists every Schuh Bade/Ngizim item plus 'Duwai. Filemaker lexical database, 1009 items' (unpublished); no Duwai phonology paper exists in it.

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 2002. Handout 04: Bade/Ngizim tones: tone system, tone rules, morphologically conditioned tones. Linguistics 252, UCLA, 10 pp.
sources.note: Bade/Ngizim two-tone system with downstep and contours; no Duwai data; 'accent' only as diacritic names. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 2002. Handouts 01, 03, 06, 07 and Course outline, Linguistics 252 'Bade and Ngizim phonology and morphology', UCLA (Handout 03 = syllable structure and the position of shwa; Handout 06 = verb classes, verbal nouns and tone).
sources.note: The only remaining unopened Schuh material on the Bade-Ngizim-Duwai group's phonology; the Internet Archive copies exist but the downloads failed today (web.archive.org connection refused intermittently). Unlikely to add a stress statement since Handouts 02 and 04 have none.

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 1981. Using dialect geography to determine prehistory: a Chadic case study. Sprache und Geschichte in Afrika 3: 201-250.
sources.note: Bade dialects + Duwai isoglosses; tone conventions in footnote 3 only; several tonal isoglosses involving Duwai (e.g. subjunctive pronouns all low with final high). No stress statement.

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 1978. Bade/Ngizim vowels and syllable structure. Studies in African Linguistics 9(3): 247-283.
sources.note: Covers Bade and Ngizim (Duwai only mentioned); tone of initial syllable discussed as a conditioning factor for prothesis; 'stress' occurs only as the verb 'I should stress'. No word-stress statement.

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 1977. Bade/Ngizim determiner system. Afroasiatic Linguistics 4(3): 1-74.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library); the library holds the journal volume but the item itself was not found; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.note: SS0.2 'Some general phonological rules' (pp. 3-5) gives tone conventions and group-wide TONE RAISING / TONE LOWERING rules for Duwai, Ngizim and three Bade dialects; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 1975. Bode, Ngodjin and Doai in the Polyglotta Africana. African Languages / Langues Africaines 1: 290-299 (posted).
sources.note: Compares Koelle's 1854 Doai (Duwai) wordlist with modern forms; only a footnote on transcription (acute = high tone, grave = low, circumflex = falling, tick = downstep). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Koelle, Sigismund Wilhelm. 1854. Polyglotta Africana. London: Church Missionary Society. (Doai = Duwai wordlist, with Koelle's accent marks.)
sources.note: Only pre-1970 record of Duwai; Koelle marked an 'accent' on each word, which Schuh 1975 reads as tone. Could be checked for whether Koelle's accent placement is stress-like, but it is a wordlist, not a description.

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. Duwai FileMaker lexical database (1009 items, 2002; expanded 2007-2009) and 1974 Gashua field notebooks, UCLA.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The underlying lexical data with tone and length marking from which the 2009 dictionary was drawn; no stress field is reported. Unpublished.

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 1971. Toward a typology of Chadic vowel and tone systems. Unpublished doctoral qualifying paper, UCLA.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Group-level prosodic typology by the only Duwai specialist; might state whether Bade-Ngizim languages have any stress alongside tone. Unpublished, not on any open host.

sources.note: Cross-linguistic survey chapter on types of tone rules (Fromkin ed. 1978, pp. 221-256) whose footnote 1, visible in the Crossref/OpenAlex record, states that its Bade and Duwai data come from Schuh's own 1973-75 Gashua field notes; it therefore contains primary Duwai tone data used to illustrate tone-rule types. Which Duwai rules and how many examples appear was not seen (record only, closed access).
